description: Problem: the installed rule ~/.omp/agent/rules/code-first.md makes the agent read the code skill at its first edit or write of a source file. Two gaps: (1) it does not fire when the agent changes source only through the shell (sed -i, redirects, python one-liners); at least four Sonnet sessions did so and none read the skill; (2) it was tested only together with a rewritten skill description, while the installed setup uses the current description, so the installed combination is untested. The scenario file of the first test was not kept. Outcome: a committed, repeatable scenario set; a measurement of the rule with the current description; and a tested decision on a shell-edit trigger. Decision gate, fixed before the runs: adopt a shell trigger only if, on Sonnet at 3 sessions per prompt, it raises loading among sessions that change source through the shell to at least 80%, fires on 0 of the near-miss sessions, and fires in 0 sessions of a new control set whose shell commands read but do not change source (grep, cat, python -m unittest, git). If the rule with the current description loads the skill in fewer of the firing sessions than 95%, report it and do not change the installed rule without the owner. If omp cannot scope a rule to shell commands, record that with evidence and close. Guardrails: (1) agents under test run only in /tmp/omp-ablation sandboxes through evals/ablation/run.py or the loading-map probe; (2) do not change ~/.omp/agent/config.yml or ~/.omp/agent/rules while sessions run, and start no run while another evaluation is running; (3) write the pre-registration (hypothesis, arms, checks, sample, decision) and commit it before any scored session; smoke runs never count; (4) use a new out folder and a ledger with the ceiling stated here; stop at the ceiling and report, do not raise it without the owner's approval; (5) read at least 5 transcripts per arm before reporting any number, and report grader faults found; (6) delete or weaken no instruction or skill text on this evidence; (7) correct an existing report with a dated note, never by silently rewriting a published number; (8) scenario and scratch code that is part of the result is committed with it; (9) publish by task branch and draft PR with identity Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>. Spend ceiling 40 USD. Extra: the rule under test lives in the sandbox repository's .omp/rules, never in the user's rules directory, during runs; the user-level rule file is changed only after the owner approves the result and when no evaluation is running; run.py already disables user rule files in sandboxes and that must stay true (check one overlay).
